title: OSPFv3 cannot select an identity after an IPv6-only rebuild
scenario: R2 was rebuilt without IPv4 addresses and reloaded. IPv6 forwarding and addressed transit Gi0/0 are configured, but the classic OSPFv3 process never establishes neighbors. The supplied excerpts are representative.

exhibits.title: R2 configuration
exhibits.text:
ipv6 unicast-routing
ipv6 router ospf 20
 passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/2
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:123::2/64
 ipv6 ospf 20 area 0
 no shutdown

exhibits.title: R2 log
exhibits.text: %OSPFv3-4-NORTRID: OSPFv3 process 20 could not pick a router-id, please configure manually

question: Which configuration gap is established by the evidence?
options: OSPFv3 requires an IPv4 address on every transit.
The IPv6-only process lacks an explicit usable router ID.
Passive Gi0/2 disables Hellos on Gi0/0 too.
The process number must equal the area number.
explanation: The log explicitly says the process cannot obtain a RID. Configure a unique 32-bit identifier; it does not have to be assigned to an IPv4 interface. The passive setting names only Gi0/2, not the transit.
fix:
```ios R2
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# ipv6 router ospf 20
R2(config-rtr)# router-id 2.2.2.2
R2(config-rtr)# end
R2# show ipv6 ospf
R2# show ipv6 ospf neighbor
R2# show ipv6 route ospf
```
This process lacked an active RID. If a different scenario has an already running process with a pending RID change, schedule any required process restart separately and expect adjacency disruption.

title: A direct adjacency disappears after a one-sided timer change
scenario: R1 and R3 share an up/up two-router link on Gi0/1. Their alternate routed path through R2 still works, but the direct OSPFv3 neighbor is absent. R3 received explicit timer overrides. These are representative interface excerpts.

exhibits.title: R1 Gi0/1
exhibits.text:
Area 0, Instance 0, RID 1.1.1.1, POINT_TO_POINT
Hello 10, Dead 40
Neighbor Count 0

exhibits.title: R3 Gi0/1
exhibits.text:
Area 0, Instance 0, RID 3.3.3.3, POINT_TO_POINT
Hello 3, Dead 12
Neighbor Count 0

question: What prevents the intended direct neighbor relationship?
options: The two interfaces use different area IDs.
The interfaces disagree on network type.
The RIDs are different from one another.
explanation: Area, instance, and intended network type agree. The effective timer pairs do not, so the Hellos do not meet the required parameters. The alternate path can mask this fault from an end-to-end ping.
fix:
```ios R3
R3# configure terminal
R3(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
R3(config-if)# no ipv6 ospf hello-interval
R3(config-if)# no ipv6 ospf dead-interval
R3(config-if)# end
R3# show ipv6 ospf interface gigabitethernet0/1
R3# show ipv6 ospf neighbor
```
Verify 10/40 at both ends and a Full direct adjacency. If a new timer pair is intentional, configure and verify both values consistently on both peers instead.
